task_name: `Pulse.tsx`: la ventana sin actividad y su llamada a la acción

rubric.result: The objective has four promises and all four are in the diff. (1) Headline with count and window: `emptyWindowBody` renders `emptyWindowHeadline(summary.window)` (Pulse.tsx:136), which format.ts:155 builds as `0 commits en ${windowLabelLong(window)}`. (2) The sentence that says it is not a failure: `emptyWindowSentence(summary.meta.lastCommitAt, now)` (Pulse.tsx:138). (3) The button that leads to 12 meses: `ctaBody` case 'switch' renders a `button` labelled `emptyWindowCtaLabel(cta.window)` whose `onClick` calls `onWindow(cta.window)` (Pulse.tsx:150-163), and App.tsx:132 wires `onWindow` to `setWindow`, whose `useEffect` on `[repoId, window]` refetches — so the click really moves the next request. (4) It does not appear on 12m: case 'already-there' returns `null`, and the already-committed `ScreenChoice.ctaFrom` answers `already-there` when `window === DEFAULT_WINDOW` ('12m'). The chart is replaced, not stacked: `activityBody` dispatches series/empty-window over the same slot.

The test the TDD line names is present verbatim (App.test.tsx:497) and its body is the assertion the plan wrote. The plan fixes: `kpis.commits: 0` on the 30-day window (the double answers `kpis: NO_COMMITS_KPIS` only for `window === '30d'`, App.test.tsx:500); the screen brings `0 commits en 30 días` (`await screen.findByText('0 commits en 30 días')`, line 512); a `Ver 12 meses` button (`getByRole('button', { name: 'Ver 12 meses' })`, line 515 — it throws if absent, so the button is asserted); and that clicking it makes the next request carry `window=12m` (`expect(urls.filter(url => url.includes('/summary?')).map(windowOf)).toEqual(['12m', '30d', '12m'])`, line 520). The strict half of the promise — that the button leads somewhere — is the one that is actually pinned, over the recorded request sequence and not over the headline alone; the earlier `findByTestId('pulse-current')` makes the click a real transition from a window that had commits.

`activity: Activity` and `onWindow: (window: TimeWindow) => void` match the Contract block name for name, in that order, with `summary: Summary` kept first (Pulse.tsx:15-20); `Activity`/`EmptyWindowCta` are imported as types from `./screen`, where task 1 committed them, and no shape is redeclared. The dispatch is over `activity.kind` ('series' | 'empty-window') and then over `cta.kind` ('switch' | 'already-there'), the two members each vocabulary declares. The one divergence is a fourth prop `now: Date` that the Contract block does not list — and the same task's prose demands it: 'frase `emptyWindowSentence` con `summary.meta.lastCommitAt` y `now`' and '`App.tsx` le pasa `activity` del miembro `blocks`, `onWindow` y el `now` que ya tiene'. I checked the plan itself (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-issue-35-estados-y-vacios.md:544-551): the Contract block there omits `now` too while its prose requires it, so this is a plan-level incompleteness the diff could only resolve one way — the alternative, Pulse reading the clock, would contradict format.ts's declared purity ('no clock reads — `relativeDays` takes `now` as a parameter') and App.tsx:29's one-instant-per-render (`const [now] = useState(() => new Date())`). Per the rule on a control or a plan text that cannot be satisfied as written, I state it here and do not count it as a finding. Everything else the brief pins — the literal `12m` target through `DEFAULT_WINDOW`, the copy functions in format.ts — is untouched and honoured.

Five rows bear on this diff and all five are implemented as closed. 'Ventana a la que apunta la llamada a la acción — `DEFAULT_WINDOW`, es decir `12m`; en esa ventana la llamada a la acción no se dibuja': the button comes from `cta.window` (never a literal), and 'already-there' returns `null`. 'Forma de esa decisión / despacho exhaustivo sin rama por defecto': `activityBody` and `ctaBody` are `switch`es with no `default`, each with a declared return type (`ReactElement`, `ReactElement | null`), so a new member breaks the build. 'Cómo se exponen los de un módulo `.tsx` que ya estaba — como su anfitrión: Pulse.tsx sigue exportando su componente por defecto': `export default function Pulse` is preserved and the new helpers follow the host's module-level idiom (the same one `App.tsx#screenBody` and `Heat.tsx#rowCells` already use). 'Dónde vive el castellano nuevo — `web/src/format.ts`': the diff adds no Spanish literal; it calls `emptyWindowHeadline`, `emptyWindowSentence` and `emptyWindowCtaLabel`. 'Quién decide qué pantalla toca / dónde vive la decisión': the empty-window trigger stays in `screen.ts#activityIn`; Pulse never reads `kpis` (`seriesBody` reads only buckets), which the block's own comment states. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: `web/src/Heat.tsx` is the named block that draws states, and it draws its own empty state exactly as this diff does — copy from format.ts (`noHeatHeadline(window)`, Heat.tsx:178) inside an inline-styled div, with module-level helpers and a default-exported component; `web/src/format.ts` keeps being the only place the Spanish appears; `web/src/App.test.tsx`'s existing `stubApi` double (including its window-function overload, already there at line 115-132) is reused rather than duplicated. defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — the subject is `Activity` and `EmptyWindowCta`, both dispatched exhaustively with no catch-all and with declared return types; the absence of a way out is a member ('already-there'), not a nullable window; no loose string or boolean is compared by hand. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: the helpers take and return typed values (`Summary`, `EmptyWindowCta`, `ReactElement`); `EMPTY_WINDOW_STYLE`/`CTA_BUTTON_STYLE` are typed `CSSProperties` handed to React, not a map logic reads by key. (3) two fields that have to agree — no new one: `activity` is not a flag repeating a field, it is the single answer computed once in `screen.ts` and the block is forbidden from re-deriving it; the empty-window state avoids the sentinel by putting the absence in `emptyWindowSentence(lastCommitAt: string | null)`, which format.ts already handled. (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: this diff raises and names no error. decisions.md: the 'window has no activity' rule is written once (`ScreenChoice.activityIn`), and the '12m is where the cta points' rule once (`ctaFrom` over `DEFAULT_WINDOW`); the diff adds no second wording of either. style.md: Pulse.tsx and App.test.tsx were already there and carry JSDoc and module-level functions — declared debt, and what is added follows the host, which is also what the closed-decisions row prescribes; the empty window is not a new concept smuggled into an old file but the second branch of the block that file is, and the brief puts it there by name. Identifiers are English, product copy Spanish, per style.md and AGENTS.md 'Code style & conventions'. architecture.md: no new module. AGENTS.md 'Security & data handling' — the new body renders headline, sentence and button only, no author identity; 'Frontera web/ ↔ server/' — no import from `server/`. No skill was named in §3, so none was loaded. Two plan-level gaps I was told about and confirmed are outside this diff's Files line, and I do not count them: the `@keyframes rp-sweep` of assumption 10 belongs to no task's Files, and `SummaryMeta.fetchedAt`/`stale` are read by no production line since freshness comes from `Clone`.

The only `-` lines in the test file are the import (widened with `Kpis`) and the mother's default `kpis: { commits: 0, activeAuthors: 0, filesTouched: 0 }` → `{ commits: 25, activeAuthors: 3, filesTouched: 12 }`. Neither touches an assertion, a case or a test, and I checked what the change does to every pre-existing test that does not override `kpis`. Three of them would have STOPPED asserting without it, because with `commits: 0` the summary now routes to the empty window and their `getByTestId('pulse-current')` would throw: 'the pulse draws the previous window behind the current one' (line 325-326, exact overlay points), 'on the full window there is no overlay' (line 344-345) and 'the heat block hangs from the right column…' (line 481). The change is what keeps them protecting the series, and it also removes an incoherent payload (buckets carrying commits while `kpis.commits` said zero). The remaining ones — the four header/freshness tests, 'a repo with no commits…' (`headSha: null`), 'changing the window asks the API for that window' and 'the full window declares there is nothing to compare' — assert on the header, the clone freshness, the URLs or `trend.reason`, none of which reads `kpis`, and I found no pre-existing assertion anywhere in the file that depended on the zeros (no test asserts `kpi-commits` off the default, and none asserts the People empty phrase 'Nadie ha tocado el repo en esta ventana.'). Nothing was relaxed or rewritten weaker; the four affected tests still assert exactly what they asserted, and the zero KPIs are now an explicit opt-in (`NO_COMMITS_KPIS`) for the tests whose case it is.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. The headline, the sentence and the button come from `web/src/Pulse.tsx` (`emptyWindowBody`, `ctaBody`) using `web/src/format.ts`; the navigation comes from `web/src/App.tsx:132` passing `onWindow: setWindow` into the body, and App's `useEffect` on `[repoId, window]` is what issues the new request. The test's double only answers `fetch` and records URLs; the `['12m','30d','12m']` sequence is a consequence of production state changes, and reverting the Pulse/App lines of this diff would make `getByRole('button', { name: 'Ver 12 meses' })` throw. No hard-coded expected value stands in for a production line.

Everything written inside the three declared files answers a sentence of the task. Pulse.tsx: the props of the Contract block plus the `now` the prose demands, the `activity` dispatch, the empty-window body 'dentro de una caja de la misma altura, para que la rejilla no salte' (`EMPTY_WINDOW_STYLE` with `height: '250px'`, the same height as the chart's svg), and the cta dispatch. The extraction of the chart into `seriesBody` (wrapped in `Fragment`) is the mechanical consequence of the dispatch the task asks for, and its body is the previous code unchanged — header, subtitle and legend untouched, as the task requires. App.tsx: the three fields added to `Shell` and the props handed to `Pulse`. App.test.tsx: the three declared test names and the constant they opt into. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched — no `Traer cambios` button, no step progress, no `Elegir otra carpeta…`, no server change, no demo chips — and no adjacent refactor, rename or extra helper appears.

Three new tests, all three properties held, so I report no finer remark and did not need to load the TDD skill. Deterministic: no assertion reads the real clock — the only clock-dependent text is the sentence in 'on the default window…', matched with `^…Su último commit fue (hoy|hace 1 día|hace \d+ días)\.$`, and `format.ts#relativeDays` only ever returns those three shapes for a past date (no month/year rollover), so the same code cannot pass today and fail later; the other two assert fixed strings and fixed SVG points; no network (fetch is stubbed), no filesystem, no randomness, no sleep. Isolated: each test creates its own double via `stubApi`, `urls` is a local array, `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in the setup file undoes the stub after each test, and nothing depends on order or on state another test left. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on rendered DOM (`0 commits en 30 días`, the full sentence, the polyline `points`, `2 cubos`) and on the literal request sequence at the fetch boundary, not on a mock's call count or a constant the test defined; each would fail if the production branch it names were wrong — including the absence assertions, which are made non-vacuous by first asserting the empty window is drawn ('on the default window…') or that the chart is drawn ('a window with commits still draws the series').
